label: heart-s2
summary: The model (training AUC 0.943) is a mostly linear risk score with three gated corrections, all added on the log-odds scale before the sigmoid. The linear part carries most of the signal (switching it off lowers the training AUC to 0.838): more vessels coloured on fluoroscopy (1.68 per sd), asymptomatic chest pain, male sex, higher cholesterol and blood pressure and a flat ST slope raise the risk. A protective gate lowers the score for younger patients with a high maximum heart rate (-1.00 log-odds on average for the 80 it acts on) and is kept shut by a reversible thallium defect (on for 3 of 90 such patients). Two stacked hinges add risk as exercise ST depression grows, faster past the second hinge, and a flat-slope gate adds risk for a flat ST segment (on for 108 of 110 flat-slope patients), less so at high cholesterol. Each leaf and the root passed its stored self-probe.
